kinds.d: Hammer with a striking face and a curved or straight claw for pulling nails.
Soft-faced or wooden-headed hammer for striking chisels and tapping parts together.
Short-handled heavy double-faced hammer for driving chisels and light demolition.
Engineer's hammer with a flat face and a rounded pein, for metalwork and riveting.
Hammer with a flat face and a wedge-shaped pein across the handle, for starting pins and tacks.
Long-handled heavy hammer swung with both hands, for demolition and driving stakes.
Hammer with a square striking face and a chisel blade, for cutting and setting bricks.
Roofer's hammer with a pointed pick, a side nail claw and a blade for cutting and holing slates.
Hardened steel rod struck with a hammer to mark centres, drive pins or set nails.
Flat or round steel bar with a curved claw end, for prying and demolition.
Thin flat steel bar with bevelled ends and nail slots, for prising trim and boards.
Short bar with a claw tip driven under a nail head to lever it out.
Long heavy straight bar with a chisel or point end, used as a lever to lift slabs and heavy items.

notes: Restraint only. Claw hammer models kept (5 market makers: Estwing, Stanley, Milwaukee, Minotaur); FatMax range dropped as repeated. Mallet: makerless 'dead blow mallet' turned into a type. Wrecking bar: makerless 'gooseneck wrecking bar' turned into a type. Pein patterns kept as kinds; pry, nail-puller and lifting bars kind-level.
